newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica's Tutu leaves hospital after cancer surgery.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica's Tutu leaves hospital after cancer surgery.

text.p: South African Nobel peace laureate Archbishop Desmond Tutu left a Cape Town hospital on Tuesday after having his cancerous prostate gland removed.
"He was discharged this morning and when he left he was in fine spirits," hospital spokeswoman Shireen Bardine said.
Doctors diagnosed the cancer last week but further tests are needed to determine if it has spread to other parts of his body.
Tutu, 65, heads South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which has the task of uncovering human rights violations during the apartheid race conflict.
Tutu will be off work for three weeks. While he was in hospital a storm of controversy broke over the commission with some black members accusing Tutu's white deputy Alex Boraine of racism.
